notes:
Gate run after each task and once more at the end; the four claims above are the final run (183 tests, 17 files). No new dependencies, no lockfile change, packages/** and examples/** untouched.

What is proven and how:
- LDT-11 states are reproduced against REAL stub servers, not a fake client (apps/studio/src/hooks/useSyrinxSession.connection.test.tsx): a bound-then-released port for refused, an http server that answers 404 and refuses every upgrade for upgrade-rejected, and a real ws server that accepts the upgrade, sends the actual session/initialization error and closes for agent-init-failed. A fourth case proves a dropped ready session is reported as a drop with its resume window, not as a failed connection.
- The Cloudflare route shape is DERIVED, never hardcoded: apps/studio/scripts/wrangler-classes.ts reads every workspace wrangler.jsonc at Vite config time and inlines the declared Durable Object class names; the kebab conversion in lib/connection-failure.ts reimplements agents/dist/utils.js camelCaseToKebabCase exactly (its all-caps and trailing-dash branches included) and is tested against it case by case. wrangler-classes.test.ts asserts against the repo's real files (finds VoiceConversation from packages/server-workers/wrangler.jsonc, excludes the studio's own assets-only worker), so a renamed class moves the UI with it. When no config is readable the panel teaches the shape and names no class.
- LDT-12's denial path is verified through the real hook with a mocked getUserMedia rejection (DOMException NotAllowedError), asserting the specific browser-permission recovery text, that status stays "connected", and that a typed turn still sends afterwards. NotFoundError is asserted as a distinct kind in the same way.
- LDT-13's done-condition is proven twice: at the hook (an injected llm.error leaves status connected, keeps the turn's transcript, and a second error does not replace the first) and at the component (AgentErrorPanel + TranscriptPanel rendered together, error shown as recoverable while the conversation stays readable).
- LDT-14's rows are folded from the ACTUAL ready message each runtime sends, transcribed from source (server-websocket/src/index.ts:359 for Node — opus downlink, both input codecs; src/edge.ts:337 for Workers — pcm_s16le, envelope always on), and one test asserts both runtimes state the identical SET of fields, which is the drift assertion.

Two defects found and fixed as root causes rather than worked around:
1. classifyMicFailure originally read error.name behind `instanceof Error`. jsdom's DOMException does not inherit Error, and neither does a cross-realm DOMException in a real browser (iframe/worker) — so a plain denial would have reported "unknown". Now read structurally off the shape.
2. A transport error event after `ready` was being classified as agent-init-failed. Classification is now gated on the session never having become ready; regression test "does not call a blip on a running session a failed start".

Behaviour changes worth flagging for review:
- A microphone the browser refuses no longer flips the session to status "error". It previously did, which left a working socket and a running agent with nothing usable — the direct cause of LDT-12's "silent screen with no recovery path". SessionView's "Waiting for microphone..." line was also changed, because it contradicted a denial that had already happened.
- Agent `error` messages are no longer mirrored into the hook's single `errorMessage` slot (which each new error erased, and which rendered the raw component name into the connection bar's prose — design rule 3). The record already keeps them all, correlated to their turn, and AgentErrorPanel is now their owner. `errorMessage` still carries transport errors.
- Connection failures are classified on the first failed attempt (the client's `reconnecting` event) rather than on `close`. The browser-client's default retry budget is 10 attempts with backoff to a 30s cap, so waiting for `close` would have left a dead port unexplained for roughly three minutes.

Not verified, and why:
- LDT-14's done-condition names BOTH a live Node and a live Cloudflare backend. I did not run either: no backend was started for this task and live smokes are the manager's step in this repo. The parity is verified against the ready shapes transcribed from the two servers' source, which catches a field one runtime omits but cannot catch a runtime whose runtime behaviour differs from its source. runs/ldt14-ready-parity-probe.mjs (pre-existing in the working tree, not written by me — mtime predates this work) is a live two-target probe that would close exactly this gap once both backends are up.
- LDT-11's reachability probe uses fetch with mode "no-cors". Its two decided branches are unit-tested with an injected fetch, and the refused/upgrade-rejected stub-server tests exercise it for real against localhost. Not exercised: a cross-origin https target where a corporate proxy or a captive portal answers for a host that is actually down, which would read as upgrade-rejected. The "unclassified" state exists so an undecidable probe never becomes a confident wrong answer, but that specific false-positive is possible.
- "audio arriving but not playing" is implemented as three separate measured conditions (server reported speech and zero frames arrived; frames arrived and every one was digital silence; frames arrived and the playback context is suspended), each distinct from silence. All are covered by component and pure-function tests. None was observed against a real backend with a genuinely broken downlink — the pair of numbers each claim rests on is real, but the claim that a codec/envelope mismatch produces exactly the first condition is reasoned from the client's decode path, not observed.
- No browser was opened. Every panel is proven by component tests over a folded SessionRecord, per the plan's verification bar; layout and visual hierarchy in SessionView are unverified beyond the build succeeding.
